A single oversized port-side engine nacelle twice the diameter of its starboard twin, raw titanium-silver against the painted hull, trailing a heat-shimmer plume that bends the star-field behind it.
A carved figurehead bolted to the bow — a crowned woman mid-scream, three meters tall, her stone-grey paint flaking to reveal gold primer beneath, facing forward into the void.
Crystalline xeno-growths clustering across the ventral hull amidships, each shard ice-blue and two meters tall, refracting engine-glow into prismatic fans across surrounding plating.
A radar mast extending from the dorsal spine longer than the ship itself, skeletal and rust-streaked, trailing four severed cable-ends that drift in micro-gravity like cut hair.
The entire starboard flank sun-bleached chalk-white while portside retains original deep crimson, the boundary between colors a razor-sharp terminator line running bow to aft.
A glasshouse observation pod jutting from the dorsal spine — hexagonal, fully-glazed, interior crammed with hanging plants and amber grow-lights visible from three hundred meters.
A five-meter diagonal gouge ripped across the portside bow, exposing four layers of structural honeycomb, the wound edges curled outward and still showing heat-blackening from impact.
Hand-painted prayer-glyphs in gold leaf running the full length of the dorsal spine, each character two meters tall, worn to ghost-traces at the bow end and vivid at the aft.
A chrome mirror-finish nose cap occupying the forward three meters, so reflective it mirrors the approaching planet in miniature, sitting garish against the matte-grey hull behind it.
Vine-overgrowth blanketing the aft engine cluster — dark green tendrils with white-tipped feelers threading through every exhaust grille, the whole mass shuddering when thrusters fire.
A docking claw armada of eleven mismatched parasite-craft clinging to the ventral hull in two ragged rows, each a different color, connected by a webwork of pressurized umbilical tubes.
A single cockpit offset hard to starboard on an otherwise centreline hull, its canopy a blister of thick yellow-tinted glass, giving the ship an unnerving one-eyed profile from the front.
Micrometeor scarring across the bow so dense the hull surface reads as hammered tin, each crater the size of a fist, glinting copper-orange under any lateral light source.
An asymmetric cooling fin on the starboard dorsal quarter, three times the height of any other fin, venting blue-white cryo-gas in a continuous plume that curls back over the hull.
A salvage hull-section grafted onto the portside amidships — darker grey, riveted with oversized bolts, its original vessel name still stenciled in red Cyrillic beneath new identifying codes.
A battery of six sensor arrays on the dorsal spine each angled differently, a bristling hedgehog cluster whose shadow-pattern rotates as the ship moves, unmistakable at any angle.
Acid-pitting across the entire ventral flank — thousands of small craters eating through three paint layers to bare metal, the pitting concentrated toward the aft and fading toward the bow.
Glowing color-changing seams tracing every hull-panel junction on the port side, cycling from blue to violet to red over ninety seconds, decorative and completely unnecessary, blazing in the dark.
A massive bombardment crater on the dorsal midship — two meters deep, eight wide, its floor patched with a single plate of bright unpainted aluminium bolted over the worst of the damage.
An external cargo container strapped to the starboard nacelle with four heavy-duty cargo straps, painted hazard-orange, stenciled with biohazard symbols, rattling visibly against its restraints.
Fungal hull-corrosion in fluorescent green-and-rust-orange blooming across the port bow, sporing filaments threading through panel seams, the largest patch shaped uncannily like a handprint.
A decorative spire rising three meters from the bow centreline — wrought in blackened steel lattice, crowned with a non-functional rotating beacon lamp, purely ceremonial and absolutely unmistakable.
A single panel on the dorsal hull painted flat vantablack while every surrounding plate gleams in standard grey, creating a rectangular absence — a hole in the ship that isn't a hole.
Nose-art painted across the portside bow in faded 1940s-style illustration — a snarling wolf's head, four meters across, one eye touched up in fresh paint while the other is ghost-pale.
A grav-rod extending eight meters from the ventral bow, thin as a lamp-post, tipped with a pulsing amber disc, casting a pale golden cone of distortion-light beneath the ship's path.
